The initial part of the ceremony interspersed the performances of various Greek singers, and featured traditional Greek dance performances from various regions of Greece (Crete, Thessaly, etc.). The event was meant to highlight the pride of the Greeks in their culture and country for the world to see.

A significant part of the closing ceremony was the exchange of the Olympic flag of the Athens Games between the mayor of Athens and the mayor of Beijing, host city of the next Olympics. After the flag exchange a presentation from the Beijing delegation presented a glimpse into Chinese culture for the world to see. Main article: [Climate of California](/wiki/Climate_of_California "Climate of California")

Further information: [Climate change in California](/wiki/Climate_change_in_California "Climate change in California")

Most of the state has a [Mediterranean climate](/wiki/Mediterranean_climate "Mediterranean climate"). The cool [California Current](/wiki/California_Current "California Current") offshore often creates summer [fog](/wiki/Fog "Fog") near the coast. Farther inland, there are colder winters and hotter summers. The maritime moderation results in the shoreline summertime temperatures of Los Angeles and [San Francisco](/wiki/San_Francisco "San Francisco") being the coolest of all major metropolitan areas of the U.S. and uniquely cool compared to areas on the same latitude in the interior and on the east coast of the North American continent. Even the [San Diego](/wiki/San_Diego "San Diego") shoreline bordering Mexico is cooler in summer than most areas in the contiguous U.S. Just a few miles inland, summer temperature extremes are significantly higher, with downtown Los Angeles being several degrees [warmer](/wiki/Climate_of_the_Los_Angeles_Basin "Climate of the Los Angeles Basin") than at the coast. The same [microclimate](/wiki/Microclimate "Microclimate") phenomenon is seen in the [climate of the Bay Area](/wiki/San_Francisco_Bay_Area#Climate "San Francisco Bay Area"), where areas sheltered from the ocean experience significantly hotter summers and colder winters in contrast with nearby areas closer to the ocean.[[135]](#cite_note-137)[[136]](#cite_note-138)[[137]](#cite_note-139)

Sent into extra innings, Jason Motte went out for his second inning of work. Elvis Andrus singled, then the Rangers' MVP candidate Josh Hamilton put Texas up again with a towering two-run home run. Down 9–7, and out of bench players, the Cardinals once again faced only three outs until elimination. Left-hander Darren Oliver came in to pitch for the Rangers to close the game. St. Louis players [Daniel Descalso](/wiki/Daniel_Descalso "Daniel Descalso") and [Jon Jay](/wiki/Jon_Jay "Jon Jay") hit back-to-back singles, and starting pitcher [Kyle Lohse](/wiki/Kyle_Lohse "Kyle Lohse") was called to bunt. Lohse's bunt went in the air, but over the head of a drawn-in Beltre, then falling for a successful sacrifice to put the tying runs in scoring position. With right-handers coming up, right-hander [Scott Feldman](/wiki/Scott_Feldman "Scott Feldman") replaced Oliver on the mound. [Ryan Theriot](/wiki/Ryan_Theriot "Ryan Theriot")'s RBI groundout scored Descalso, cutting the Rangers' lead to 9–8, and following an intentional walk to Pujols, Berkman stepped up to the plate. Feldman got ahead on the count 1–2 on a foul ball. Berkman worked the count to 2–2, and the Rangers were once again one strike away from their first championship title. Berkman then smacked Feldman's next pitch into center field for a single, scoring Jay and tying the game once again. It was the first time in World Series history that a team came back from two different two-run deficits in the ninth inning or later in the same game.[[45]](#cite_note-45). But again, despite Berkman advancing to second on defensive indifference and having the winning run on third in Pujols, the Cardinals failed to score when Craig grounded out to end the inning.

The Rangers failed to score in the top of the 11th against [Jake Westbrook](/wiki/Jake_Westbrook "Jake Westbrook"), who worked around a one-out single from Napoli. This brought David Freese to lead off the bottom of the inning against new Rangers reliever [Mark Lowe](/wiki/Mark_Lowe "Mark Lowe"), who had relieved Feldman. With a worldwide box-office gross of over $2.9 billion, *Avatar* is proclaimed to be the "highest-grossing" film, but such claims usually refer to [theatrical](/wiki/Movie_theatre "Movie theatre") revenues only and do not take into account [home video](/wiki/Home_video "Home video") and [television](/wiki/Television "Television") income, which can form a significant portion of a film's earnings. Once revenue from home entertainment is factored in, it is not immediately clear which film is the most successful. *[Titanic](/wiki/Titanic_(1997_film) "Titanic (1997 film)")* earned $1.2 billion from [video](/wiki/Video "Video") and [DVD](/wiki/DVD-Video "DVD-Video") sales and rentals,[[1]](#cite_note-titanic-sales-1) in addition to the $2.2 billion it grossed in theaters. While complete sales data are not available for *Avatar*, it earned $345 million from the sale of sixteen million DVD and [Blu-ray](/wiki/Blu-ray "Blu-ray") units in North America,[[2]](#cite_note-2) and ultimately sold a total of thirty million DVD and Blu-ray units worldwide.[[3]](#cite_note-3) After home video income is accounted for, both films have earned over $3 billion each. Television [broadcast](/wiki/Broadcasting "Broadcasting") rights also substantially add to a film's earnings and, as of 2010, a film often earned the equivalent of as much as 20–25% of its theatrical box office for two television runs, on top of [pay-per-view](/wiki/Pay-per-view "Pay-per-view") revenues;[[4]](#cite_note-4) *Titanic* earned a further $55 million from the [NBC](/wiki/NBC "NBC") and [HBO](/wiki/HBO "HBO") broadcast rights,[[1]](#cite_note-titanic-sales-1) equating to about 9% of its North American gross.

The Bordeaux wine region accounts for more than 60% of the Cabernet Sauvignon grown in France. Cabernet Sauvignon wines are generally lighter and less structured, drinkable much earlier than Bordeaux wine. In the southwest French *[appellation d'origine contrôlée](/wiki/Appellation_d%27origine_contr%C3%B4l%C3%A9e "Appellation d'origine contrôlée")* (AOCs) of [Bergerac](/wiki/Bergerac_AOC "Bergerac AOC") and [Buzet](/wiki/Buzet_AOC "Buzet AOC") it is used to make [rosé](/wiki/Ros%C3%A9 "Rosé") wine. In some regions, it is used to add flavour and structure to [Carignan](/wiki/Carignan "Carignan") while it is blended with [Négrette](/wiki/N%C3%A9grette "Négrette") in [Gaillac](/wiki/Gaillac_(AOC) "Gaillac (AOC)") and [Fronton](/wiki/Fronton,_Haute-Garonne "Fronton, Haute-Garonne") as well as [Tannat](/wiki/Tannat "Tannat") in [Madiran](/wiki/Madiran_wine "Madiran wine"). In August 2019, Governor [Ned Lamont](/wiki/Ned_Lamont "Ned Lamont") appointed Cardona as [commissioner of education](/wiki/Connecticut_State_Department_of_Education "Connecticut State Department of Education"); Cardona was the first Latino to hold the position.[[12]](#cite_note-csde-12)[[11]](#cite_note-ctmirror.org-11) During his tenure, Cardona helped oversee state schools' response to the [COVID-19 pandemic](/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Connecticut "COVID-19 pandemic in Connecticut"), where he expressed concerns over the long-term mental health impacts of [remote education](/wiki/Remote_education "Remote education") on students.[[8]](#cite_note-:3-8)

These have prograde and nearly circular orbits of low inclination and are split into two groups:

* ***Inner satellites*** or ***Amalthea group***: [Metis](/wiki/Metis_(moon) "Metis (moon)"), [Adrastea](/wiki/Adrastea_(moon) "Adrastea (moon)"), [Amalthea](/wiki/Amalthea_(moon) "Amalthea (moon)"), and [Thebe](/wiki/Thebe_(moon) "Thebe (moon)"). These orbit very close to Jupiter; the innermost two orbit in less than a Jovian day. The latter two are respectively the fifth and seventh largest moons in the Jovian system. Observations suggest that at least the largest member, Amalthea, did not form on its present orbit, but farther from the planet, or that it is a captured Solar System body.[[62]](#cite_note-63) These moons, along with a number of seen and as-yet-unseen inner moonlets (see [Amalthea moonlets](/wiki/Amalthea_moonlets "Amalthea moonlets")), replenish and maintain Jupiter's faint [ring system](/wiki/Rings_of_Jupiter "Rings of Jupiter"). Metis and Adrastea help to maintain Jupiter's main ring, whereas Amalthea and Thebe each maintain their own faint outer rings.[[63]](#cite_note-list-64)[[64]](#cite_note-65)
* ***Main group*** or ***[Galilean moons](/wiki/Galilean_moons "Galilean moons")***: [Io](/wiki/Io_(moon) "Io (moon)"), [Europa](/wiki/Europa_(moon) "Europa (moon)"), [Ganymede](/wiki/Ganymede_(moon) "Ganymede (moon)") and [Callisto](/wiki/Callisto_(moon) "Callisto (moon)"). They are some of [the largest objects](/wiki/List_of_moons "List of moons") in the [Solar System](/wiki/Solar_System "Solar System") outside the [Sun](/wiki/Sun "Sun") and the eight planets in terms of mass, larger than any known [dwarf planet](/wiki/Dwarf_planet "Dwarf planet").
